info.title: Seylo API
info.description: Every action in the Seylo panel. Queries are GET requests with query parameters; everything else is a POST with a JSON body. Docs: https://docs.seylo.dev

post.description: Stops the reply that is streaming in a conversation. Text so far is kept; the message ends with status cancelled.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's conversations with all its messages; a reply still streaming comes with its text so far. Another person's conversation is NOT_FOUND.
Lists the caller's assistant conversations, most recently active first; nobody sees anyone else's, not even owners. query keeps the ones whose title holds it.

post.description: Deletes one of the caller's conversations and its messages. Usage records stay for the bill.

get.description: Says whether the caller can use the assistant (and why not), whether the Assistant page is on, the caller's auto mode and whether this month's budget is used up.

post.description: Changes the title of one of the caller's conversations (set from the first message when it starts).

post.summary: Try the assistant's last reply again
post.description: Starts a new reply after the conversation's last one failed or was stopped; the failed reply stays as it was. Returns at once; the reply streams like ai.send's. CONFLICT while a reply is streaming or when the last reply did not fail.

post.summary: Send a message to the AI assistant
post.description: Adds the person's message (to a new conversation when conversationId is left out) and starts the assistant's reply. Returns at once; the reply streams on the live topic ai:<conversationId>. Fails with CONFLICT while a reply is still streaming and with FORBIDDEN once the monthly budget is reached.

post.summary: Turn the assistant's auto mode on or off
post.description: Sets the caller's auto mode for every chat and device. On, the assistant runs changes in the caller's chats without an approval, as the caller and with the caller's own permissions (audited with autoMode); off, every change waits in Approvals. Only from the browser: API keys get FORBIDDEN.

get.description: Returns whether the assistant is on, whether a key is stored, the model routing and the monthly budget.

post.description: Changes the assistant settings. anthropicApiKey stores a new key (sealed; null removes it); omitted fields keep their value. The key is checked with a cheap request before it is saved.

get.summary: Get AI usage and the projected bill
get.description: Returns token use and cost for a month (default the current one, UTC) by model, by day and by person, the budget, and the bill projected from the pace so far.
Lists alerts newest first, limited to the projects, services and nodes the caller can see. Filter by project, service or node; page with the nextCursor of the previous call.

post.description: Stops notifications for a scope (everything, a project, a service or a node), optionally for one event only and until a time. Alerts keep being recorded in the feed.

get.description: Lists the mutes that are still in effect. Muted alerts still appear in the feed, marked muted, but no channel is notified.

post.description: Ends a mute now so its scope notifies again.

Creates an API key or MCP token for the signed-in person, limited to the given actions ("*" for all of yours), optionally to some projects, read-only or not, with an optional expiry. The token is returned once. Browser sessions only, signed in or confirmed with auth.reauth in the last 15 minutes (FORBIDDEN details.reason "reauth" otherwise).

expiresInDays.description: Leave out for a key that never expires.

get.description: Lists the signed-in person's API keys and MCP tokens, newest first. Owners and admins can pass all=true to see everyone's keys.

post.description: Makes a key or MCP token stop working right away. Your own keys, or anyone's for owners and admins.

get.description: Returns the signed-in person's UI preferences (hidden projects, whether the sidebar shows them, the sidebar items they turned off, color mode and similar).

preferences.description: Per-person UI choices that follow them across browsers, for example hidden projects or color mode. Keys not listed here are free-form.

hiddenProjectIds.description: Projects hidden from this person's sidebar and home page, by id. Only projects the person can see are kept; deleted projects drop out. The project pages, links and search still show them.

showHiddenInSidebar.description: Whether this person's sidebar shows the folded "Hidden (N)" group of hidden projects. Missing means true (the default); only false is stored. Hidden projects still show on the home page under "Show hidden", in search and at their links either way.

hiddenSidebarItems.description: Main navigation items this person took out of their sidebar. Missing means none: every item shows. Settings never hides, and Approvals still shows while a request waits for the person. The pages still open at their links and from search.

post.description: Confirms the signed-in person with exactly one of: the password, a code (6-digit authenticator code or an unused recovery code, which is used up), or a passkey assertion for the ticket from auth.reauthPasskeyBegin. The session then counts as freshly signed in for 15 minutes. A wrong answer is BAD_REQUEST with details.field "password", "code" or "passkey". A linked GitHub login confirms through auth.reauthGithubStart instead. Browser sessions only.

Polls the device flow started by auth.reauthGithubStart. With status done GitHub approved it as the login linked to this account, and the session counts as freshly signed in for 15 minutes (freshUntil), as after auth.reauth. Approving as another GitHub login is BAD_REQUEST with details.field "github" and counts toward the per-address lock; an unknown, used or expired ticket is BAD_REQUEST. Browser sessions only.

post.summary: Start confirming it's you with GitHub
post.description: Starts the GitHub device flow to confirm the signed-in person with the GitHub login linked to their account, for accounts that sign in with GitHub. Show userCode, open verificationUri, then call auth.reauthGithubPoll every intervalSeconds. CONFLICT when the account has no linked GitHub login, UNAVAILABLE while the OAuth client id is a placeholder. Browser sessions only.

post.summary: Start confirming it's you with a passkey
post.description: Returns WebAuthn request options for navigator.credentials.get, limited to the signed-in person's passkeys, and a ticket for auth.reauth. UNAVAILABLE without a panel domain, CONFLICT when the account has no passkey.
Replaces every recovery code with 10 new ones, shown once. Needs a current authenticator code. Only while 2FA is on.
Ends every session of the signed-in person except the current one.
Ends one of your own sessions, for example a browser you no longer use. Ending the current one is the same as signing out.

get.description: Returns how the signed-in person can sign in: password, authenticator app (TOTP), recovery codes left, passkeys and a linked GitHub login.

post.description: Checks a code from the newly enrolled authenticator, turns 2FA on and returns 10 recovery codes. They are shown once; store them somewhere safe.
Turns 2FA off and deletes the recovery codes. Needs a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code.

post.summary: Start setting up an authenticator app
post.description: Creates a new TOTP secret for the signed-in person and returns it as a QR-ready otpauth URL. It is not enforced until auth.totpConfirm. CONFLICT when 2FA is already on. Needs a sign-in or auth.reauth from the last 15 minutes (FORBIDDEN details.reason "reauth" otherwise).

post.description: Adds an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO) for backups. Run backups.testDestination first to check the keys.
Schedules backups of a service's database or one of its volumes to a destination, keeping the newest keepLast. Database services back up with the engine's dump tool; volumes as a tar.zst archive.
Removes a destination from the panel. Fails while a schedule still writes to it. Objects already in the bucket are not deleted, but the panel can no longer restore them.
Stops a schedule. Backups it already made stay in the bucket and in the run list until deleted.
Deletes a backup's object from the bucket and marks the run deleted. It can no longer be restored.

get.description: Lists the panel's S3/R2 backup destinations. Owners and admins get every field; other signed-in people with a grant (services.view or backups.edit somewhere) get only id, name, provider and bucket in the choices list, for picking one in a schedule; an account with no grant gets empty lists.
Lists the backup schedules of a service (its database, or each volume) with the next run time and the last result.
Lists a service's backup and restore runs, newest first, 50 per page. Pass the last run's startedAt as before for the next page.

post.description: Restores a successful backup over the service's current data (database or volume). Current data is replaced and cannot be recovered unless backed up first. The service name must be repeated to confirm.
Starts a backup right away: of a schedule (policyId), or a one-off of the database or a volume to a destination. Returns the run; follow it with backups.listRuns or the live service topic.

Writes, reads and deletes a small test object to check the endpoint, bucket and keys. Test a saved destination by id, or unsaved settings with draft (a draft without secretAccessKey reuses the saved key of destinationId).
Changes a destination. Fields left out keep their value, including the secret key. Existing backups stay where they were written.
Changes a schedule's destination, timing, retention or on/off state. Fields left out keep their value.

post.summary: Serve the panel on the tailnet
post.description: Adds or removes the one Tailscale Serve entry that sends https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net to the panel. Nothing restarts and nothing closes. Turning it on needs the owner from a browser session with a fresh sign-in, and a server that is signed in, new enough and has MagicDNS on (CONFLICT details.reason one of serveBlockedReasons otherwise). It serves the panel on the tailnet the server is signed in to then, and on no other: when the server signs in to another tailnet the entry goes until the owner turns Serve on again for that one. Turning it off while it is the only working way in and IP access is closed reopens IP access ("reopen" mode, reopenedUrl says where), or is CONFLICT in "stayClosed" mode unless reopenIpAccess is true.

post.summary: Get a Tailscale sign-in link for the server
post.description: Asks the server's tailscaled for an interactive sign-in link. Whoever opens it puts the server on their tailnet, so only the owner gets it, from a browser session with a fresh sign-in, and only while the server is not signed in (a stopped server is signed in: CONFLICT details.reason 'stopped', start it on the server). The first sign-in from the panel turns Tailscale DNS off on the server. The link is kept in memory for 10 minutes and never stored or audited.
